name: Beijing Capital
stand: The public perimeter the guide still marks as open.
when: When the wind keeps arrivals on the near runway.
note: Stay on the public side of the fence. The field is not a place to wander off the marked path.

name: Beijing Daxing
stand: The public edge the guide lists for the arrival pair.
when: Clear days, when the long final is readable from the road.
note: Daxing is new and tightly kept. Use only the public places the guide names.

name: Shanghai Pudong
stand: The public roadside the guide still lists.
when: When arrivals are on the runway nearest that road.
note: Pudong's public spots are specific. The rest of the perimeter is not a viewing place.

name: Guangzhou
stand: The public side of the arrival runway.
when: Afternoon light on the near final.
note: Stay where the public can already stand. Do not cross into the airport's own land.

name: Tokyo Haneda
stand: The public park and the observation deck that are open to visitors.
when: When the deck is open and the wind favours the near runway.
note: Haneda keeps a real public deck. Use that, not the fence.

name: Tokyo Narita
stand: The public park along the approach.
when: Daylight arrivals on the runway the park faces.
note: The park is the place. The rest of the boundary is not.

name: Seoul Incheon
stand: Only the public places the guide still names.
note: Incheon is strict. If a place is not listed as public, it is not a spot.

name: Singapore Changi
stand: The public viewing mall and the listed roadside.
note: Changi's own viewing floor is the straightforward place. Roadside spots are the ones the guide still lists.

name: Bangkok Suvarnabhumi
stand: The public side the guide names, and nowhere else.
when: Daylight, away from the restricted roads.
note: Use the listed public side. The airport roads are not a viewing place.

name: London Heathrow
stand: Myrtle Avenue for 27L, and the public parks for the other arrival.
when: When the wind is on the runway that park faces.
note: Heathrow's classic public places are still the parks and Myrtle Avenue, not the perimeter road.

name: Frankfurt
stand: The public observation deck and the listed visitor points.
note: Frankfurt keeps a visitor deck. Start there.

name: Los Angeles
stand: The In-N-Out terrace and the Imperial Hill park.
when: West-flow afternoons, when the light is on the arrivals.
note: The restaurant terrace and Imperial Hill are the public places. The rest of the loop is a road.

name: Dubai
stand: Only a listed public place, if one is open.
when: When that place is open to visitors.
note: Dubai is not a fence-spotting field. Use a public place or skip it.
